name: BMS / Control System — power-up and I/O-check before sequence and integration testing

activities: install DDC/controller panels, PLC cabinets and marshalling
terminate field I/O from sensors, valves, dampers and actuators into controllers
sequence.note: Interfaces instrumentation and HVAC/mechanical field devices.

activities: third-party integrations via gateways (chillers, gensets, meters, fire, lifts)
control sequences per narrative: PID loops, staging, interlocks
cross-system cause-and-effect: fire shutdown, smoke control, generator, metering, lifts

typical_relationships.reason: panels need the finished, environmentally controlled room and plinths
terminations land inside the mounted panels
I/O can only be read once controllers are live and communicating
each point verifies a real field device back to the controller
sequences are meaningless until each point is proven true
BMS sequences must drive real, runnable plant
cause-and-effect needs each interfacing system commissioned first

interfaces.requirement: field I/O and loop checks provide the points the BMS reads and commands
sequence testing requires the mechanical plant installed and motor-ready to control
plant staging/sequencing requires the chilled-water system installed and fillable
fire shutdown/smoke-control interface (hardwired plus gateway) must be live for integration test
control-network cabling and backbone in place

testing_requirements: Control-sequence functional performance test per control narrative
commissioning_dependencies: Field devices installed, calibrated and loop-checked (instrumentation)
Mechanical/electrical plant installed and ready to run
Approved control narrative / points list / cause-and-effect matrix
Software and graphics downloaded and backed up
typical_exceptions: Packaged plant with its own controls integrated by gateway only
Pre-configured/virtualized controllers reduce on-site software scope
evidence: Control-sequence functional testing was scheduled before the field I/O point-to-point checks and before the mechanical plant it controls was installed, and cross-system integration was booked before the fire-alarm interface was live.
